L2t: Skeletal muscle fibres contract in response to signals from motor neurons at the neuromuscular junction.
L3t: Contraction is maintained only while the motor neuron keeps releasing acetylcholine, so relaxation follows once that signal stops and calcium is pumped back into the sarcoplasmic reticulum.
L4t: A muscle fibre relaxes when the nerve stimulus is removed.
L2f: Skeletal muscle fibres contract in response to signals from sensory neurons that bypass the neuromuscular junction.
L3f: Muscle fibres have a built-in safety mechanism that shuts down contraction whenever the incoming nerve signal exceeds a certain intensity, causing the fibre to go slack.
L4f: A muscle fibre relaxes when the nerve stimulus is too forceful.
cand_wrong1: the nerve stimulus is too forceful
cand_wrong2: the muscle fibre runs out of oxygen
